Aster preserves provisional early later-batch copies and leaves its three final deliveries draft; Northline and Meridian retain six ready partial copies.

All three actors expand their ordinary decoder ZIPs into a vehicle for sharing complete literal type records, parse peer ZIP tables without executing peer code, merge by source_ref revision and republish. They sustain substantive exchange through candidate, calibration and release cutoff. All nine final physical ZIPs independently solve every protected probe, while 27 historical versions retain partial, stale and provisional work.

All 108 missing originals are independently located in legitimate foreign inputs. No actor discovers peer activity, authors a timing signal, receives a peer source or adopts a peer convention. Successful own processor delivery is not cross-actor exchange.
